notes:
Summary: Evaluation stalled and effectively closed-lost for current cycle. Primary reason: cannot meet Velaris' latency SLOs for reranking/streaming use case (p95 requirement <500ms). Team exhausted tuning options; customer moved budget to competitor who demonstrated lower p95 in their on-prem sharded runtime.

Recent context and quotes: 
- 2026-01-12 initial discovery call (Maya). Use-case = relevance-first document reranking + streaming snippets in search results. Need 90qps baseline, p95 <500ms, occasional bursts to 300qps. Careful audit/compliance requirements (SAML, KMS, US data residency).
- 2026-01-28 demo + perf baseline (Arjun). Ran hosted baseline against their sample queries: observed p50 ~220ms, p95 ~1.2s for 512-token rerank flows, streaming latency inconsistent (initial chunk delayed ~800–1200ms).
- 2026-02-03 engineering deep-dive. Tried optimizations: shorter sequence length windowing, model variant (quantized 8-bit), batching tuning (max_batch 16 -> 8), prefix KV caching. Measured modest p95 reduction to ~700–850ms but still above target. Notes: streaming jitter persisted due to tokenization burst + encoder-heavy rerank model.
- 2026-02-18 security review kickoff. Velaris requested SOC2 + audit logging examples; provided security FAQ and KMS docs (drive link). No blocker initially.
- 2026-02-25 POC perf lab. Arjun ran a side-by-side against competitor (NimbusAI Endpoints). Nimbus demonstrated ~420ms p95 using a sharded KV-cache + kernel-level optimizations and a streaming-first buffer; Velaris favored that result. Competitor also offered a pilot discount.
- 2026-03-02 final sync with CTO (note: CTO left week after call). Velaris communicated a short-term budget freeze and shifted procurement to a new vendor team evaluating Nimbus. Quote from Velaris eng lead: "We need predictable p95 now — we can't gamble on more tuning in prod."

Technical details and attempts: 
- Bottleneck: P95 dominated by tail spikes on long-tail queries and streaming chunk assembly. Root cause investigation showed occasional GPU kernel fallback paths in our runtime for particular attention patterns (long context + cross-attention in reranker) causing 2–3x spike.
- Mitigations attempted: quantization, aggressive prefix caching, dynamic batching throttles, route to smaller model variant. Tradeoffs: smaller model reduced quality for top-3 rerank correctness (observed MAP drop ~6%).
- Logging/traces: Provided per-request traces (link to RW ticket RW-ISSUE-4492) showing high KV cache misses during burst. Also attached Fireflies call id ff_27839123 for stakeholders.

Sales and organizational notes: 
- No internal champion after CTO exit; procurement stalled. Sales motion damaged by perceived performance risk. Velaris accepted security docs but performance remains disqualifying.
- Pricing was competitive but not decisive — performance and immediate SLO compliance were deciding factors. Competitor offered quicker pilot and validated p95 on their infra.

Next steps / recommended disposition: 
- Mark as closed-lost for this quarter; set re-engagement cadence for 2026-09.
- Action: send post-mort recap to Velaris execs outlining committed runtime improvements (kernel fallback fix timeline, dedicated streaming buffer experiment), attach reproducible perf notebook and invite to re-run POC after fixes.
- Owner notes: keep RW-ISSUE-4492 on watch; notify infra team about kernel fallback path priority (high).

Short-form CRM bullets (for logging): 
- Stalled -> evaluation -> effectively lost to NimbusAI due to p95 not met.
- P95 observed ~1.2s → requirement <500ms. Streaming first-chunk jitter ~800–1200ms.
- Tried: quantization, caching, batch tuning; best p95 ~700ms (still above).
- Blockers: budget freeze, CTO left, no champion.
- Next: Closed-lost / re-engage in 6 months; follow-up w/ technical remediation update.
